key_insight: ORCA-bench shows that frontier language model agents are still far from reliable on production-style oncall root cause analysis, even with access to telemetry and source code.
engineering_relevance: For SRE and platform teams, the results suggest agentic debugging tools need much stronger reasoning and incident-context handling before they can be trusted for real operational response.
method: Built a production-fidelity microservice testbed with OpenTelemetry instrumentation and six days of metrics, logs, and traces.
Created 1,079 RCA tasks with varying report specificity, detection delay, and co-occurring faults.
Evaluated frontier coding agents using real telemetry interfaces plus full source-code access.
evidence_signal: The benchmark was curated by expert SREs and validated with human rescoring of the LLM judge (weighted Cohen’s kappa = 0.90), with best RCA accuracy only 25.3% on Medium tasks and 10.0% on Hard.
watch_item: Performance is measured on a curated 50 GB, six-day testbed, so real production systems may be even harder and results may underestimate the deployment gap.
paper_title: ORCA-bench: How Ready Are Language Model Agents for Oncall?
